Countably many rational-time distance functions are scalar absolutely continuous and have derivatives bounded by an L2 control. Their derivative supremum is measurable and controls every increment by density. Differentiating its indefinite integral bounds the upper metric difference quotient, while each distance derivative bounds the lower quotient. This proves two-sided a.e. existence and leastness without endpoints or circular use of minimal velocity.
